context: Six-panel small-multiples showing network evolution over 6 months, each panel an independent force-directed layout with ~14-19 nodes and ~21-24 edges, encoding edge status as green (new), pink dashed (removed), or gray (persistent).
first_impression: Readable at a glance within each panel, but the independent force simulations mean node positions are random across months, so the 'evolution' framing is undercut — you cannot track any node's trajectory over time.
what_works: Panel count (6) and per-panel density (~17 nodes, sparse edges) are both comfortably below overload thresholds; the three-status edge color scheme (green/pink/gray) is immediately legible with minimal legend lookup.
what_doesnt: Independent simulations produce inconsistent node positions across panels, defeating the temporal comparison the visualization promises — a viewer cannot follow a specific node's neighborhood as it evolves; isolated nodes that drift far from the main cluster (visible in February, March, April) fragment spatial attention and waste panel area without adding information.
